classification.difficultyReason: Direct application of the taught input-absolute-value transformation: recognise f(|x|), retain the nonnegative-x branch and identify its reflection. No unsignposted connection or linked procedure is essential.

content.prompt: The graph of $f(x)=x(x+2)^2$ is shown as a dotted line. Which represents $y=|x|(|x|+2)^2$?

spec.description: Four-option row, option A. Black dashed base cubic and black solid symmetric nonnegative distractor; no grid, point markers or origin label.
spec.mathematics: The dashed curve is f(x)=x(x+2)^2. The graphical distractor has zeros at -2, 0 and 2, smooth minima at -2 and 2, a sharp minimum at 0, intervening positive humps and rising outer branches. Its unlabelled shape is reconstructed with editable Bézier paths without assigning an unsupported equation or exact hump coordinates.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and the option label are permanent question content.

spec.description: Four-option row, option B. Black dashed base cubic and black solid nonnegative distractor; no grid, point markers or origin label.
spec.mathematics: The dashed curve is f(x)=x(x+2)^2. The graphical distractor descends steeply from the upper left to a sharp minimum at 0, has a positive hump between 0 and 2, a smooth minimum at 2 and a rising right branch. Unlabelled distractor shapes are editable Bézier paths, without an asserted exact equation.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and the option label are permanent question content.

spec.description: Four-option row, option C. Black dashed base cubic and black solid symmetric nonnegative transformed curve; no grid, point markers or origin label.
spec.mathematics: Dashed base f(x)=x(x+2)^2. Solid curve y=|x|(|x|+2)^2 is plotted from its equation. It has a sharp minimum at the origin, steep curved branches on both sides and no other zeros. The solid right branch coincides with the base cubic and is drawn over it.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and the option label are permanent question content; no correctness annotation is printed.

spec.description: Four-option row, option D. Black dashed base cubic and black solid nonnegative distractor; no grid, point markers or origin label.
spec.mathematics: The dashed curve is f(x)=x(x+2)^2. The solid distractor has a smooth minimum at -2, a positive hump between -2 and 0, a sharp minimum at the origin and rising outer branches. The unlabelled left shape uses an editable Bézier path; the right branch is plotted from the known base equation where the source curves coincide.
spec.answerVisibility: Both curves and the option label are permanent question content.

answer.worked: This is $y=f(|x|)$. Keep the graph on and to the right of the $y$-axis, remove the original left-hand branch, and reflect the right-hand branch across the $y$-axis. The resulting graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis and has its only zero at the origin. Correct answer: C.
